items.prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Edit the provided full-body overhead triceps starting pose photograph ONLY to provide a farther camera framing for a consistent two-frame exercise sequence. Preserve exactly the woman, pose, face, ponytail, white T shirt, charcoal long pants, white sneakers, small gray dumbbell, blue-gray studio lighting/background. The RIGHT upper arm is vertical overhead, RIGHT elbow bent and small dumbbell behind the head without touching it, own LEFT hand gently supporting the right upper arm across the chest. Keep her neutral standing trunk, two feet fixed on the floor, natural joints, clear grip and the complete dumbbell. Zoom the camera OUT so the woman's STANDING stature measured from top of HEAD to floor is only about 70% of total canvas HEIGHT, not 88%. Keep the shoes baseline at about 94% of image height; head top should therefore be near 24% of image height, not near the upper edge. The bent elbow is allowed a little above her head, but there MUST be large empty blue-gray space over her raised elbow and weight to permit subsequent straight-arm extension overhead with at least 8% top margin. The normal human height and limb lengths must remain proportional: achieve this through camera distance, never by shortening the head or legs. Keep original near-right-side three-quarter perspective and the same single bent elbow starting pose. Single full-body 4:5 portrait image. No text, labels, panels, arrows, logos, second person or extra objects. Do not change the exercise to an extended elbow yet.

visual_check.support: 两肩肘腕连接正常，双足完整落地
visual_check.composition: 统一拉远构图，头顶约355px，足底约1280px，留出伸肘所需上方空间

items.prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Precisely edit the attached photograph from step 01 to step 02 of supported right-arm overhead elbow extension. MODIFY ONLY the RIGHT forearm, right wrist/right hand, and the small gray dumbbell so that the RIGHT ELBOW extends from its bent position to a near straight position, moving the hand and dumbbell UPWARD above that elbow. Keep the RIGHT UPPER ARM in its exact existing position, almost vertical, shoulder and elbow centers unchanged. Her OWN LEFT hand gently supports the same right upper arm at the exact current contact point. All other regions must be identical to the reference: head and face top at the same height, neck, shoulders, support arm and fingers, white shirt, torso, hips, legs, white shoes in the EXACT same position and size, feet on the EXACT same floor baseline, blue-gray background, shadows and original 4:5 canvas size. Do NOT zoom, resize, reframe, shift the person downward or change standing posture. The existing reference has ample empty space above the bent elbow; use this space for the extended forearm and dumbbell, retaining at least 6% empty image height above the dumbbell. Keep natural upper-arm/forearm lengths and neutral right wrist, grip the same small gray dumbbell centrally, both gray ends fully visible. Calm right-facing gaze, ribs and pelvis upright, no leaning back. This is single-joint elbow extension with unchanged shoulder position, never a shoulder press. Preserve full-body composition with both soles grounded. Single pose, no panels, text, arrows, logos or watermark.

discarded_candidates.prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Asset: one standalone realistic rehabilitation demonstration photograph, step 02 of a supported right-arm overhead triceps elbow extension. Image 1 is the precise scene/composition/identity and step 01 pose reference; images 2-4 are the same person's identity and studio style references. Modify image 1 to the end of elbow extension while preserving the exact woman, face, black ponytail, white short-sleeved T-shirt, dark gray long pants, white trainers, light gray-blue seamless studio floor and background, soft shadows, three-quarter right-facing side camera, camera distance, framing and body scale. Show one woman standing on both planted feet, torso upright neutral, pelvis and ribs stacked, no arching or leaning. Keep the RIGHT upper arm in the SAME near vertical overhead position and the LEFT hand gently supporting the same right upper arm near its lower portion. Straighten the RIGHT elbow so the forearm extends upward in line with the near-vertical upper arm; the right hand firmly grips the SAME small gray dumbbell by its middle handle above the right elbow and above the head. This is elbow extension, not a shoulder press: the shoulder/upper arm position must remain almost fixed while the bent forearm in image 1 rotates upward. The support arm is her OWN left arm connected naturally to her left shoulder across her chest, and the left hand stays at the same upper arm contact. Right wrist neutral, elbow visually continuous; show the complete dumbbell and both ends clearly with plenty of room at the top. Head looks calmly forward right. Full-body 4:5 vertical composition showing all fingers, full shoes and floor contacts with natural anatomy and limb proportions. One single pose only; no panels, labels, text, arrows, logos or watermark. Do not add any other person or equipment. Do not crop the raised dumbbell. Preserve the grayscale dumbbell's size and shape from image 1.
